pictures.scene: Munkacsy, Christ Before Pilate — a packed judgment hall with a great stone arch and dark panelled walls climbing away above everyone's heads, the Lord standing alone in the middle of the floor in a plain white robe, barefoot, His wrists tied in front of Him and His face lifted and turned quietly to the left, a man in a white headcloth and black gown leaning far out over the rail behind Him with his whole arm flung out and one finger pointing at Him, a Roman soldier in a red cloak and a steel helmet holding a spear level across the front of the picture, a rich old man in a scarlet robe and a yellow turban sprawled on a bench at the right watching with his chin down, rows of bearded accusers crowded shoulder to shoulder behind, and a woman with a child in her arms standing against the pillar looking on, then the whole council rose and led jesus away to pilate, …
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_christ_before_pilate

pictures.scene: Delaroche, The Interrogation — a cold stone cell almost black above, an old judge in a scarlet cape and scarlet cap seated heavily at the left with a gold cross on his breast, his head twisted round and his lip curled as he stares across at his prisoner, one bare hand hanging open over his knee, and at the right a young prisoner in a plain white shift and dark sleeves sitting up on a heap of straw with an iron chain locked round her wrists, her fingers knotted together and her face lifted calm and tired toward him, a clerk's arm with a quill and a sheet of paper just showing in the dark behind the judge's shoulder, so pilate asked him, are you the king of the jews, you have said so, jesus replied, …
pictures.name: pd_delaroche_verhoor

pictures.scene: Brueghel, The Sermon on the Mount — a huge shady wood of green and gold leaved trees filling the whole upper half with a glimpse of pale sky at the top left, and under it a vast crowd packed across the clearing, hundreds of small figures in blue and red and black, the Teacher standing small in the middle of them on a low rise in a pale robe with a thin gold halo and both hands open as He speaks, rows of listeners seated and standing all round Him, farmers in hats, women in white headcloths with babies, townsmen in dark cloaks and ruffs, a girl in a yellow satin dress sitting on the grass in the near corner with a little dog beside her, and more people still coming in along the edges of the trees, but they kept insisting, he stirs up the people all over judea with his teaching, he began in galilee and has come all the way here, …
pictures.name: pd_brueghel_bergrede

pictures.scene: Gentileschi, Esther Before Ahasuerus — a young king lolling sideways on a gilded throne set up on a pale stone dais, a spiked gold crown pinned to a black plumed cap on his dark curls, his face in clean profile with the eyes swivelled round to stare at someone outside the picture, a rose silk sash across a black doublet buttoned with gold, a huge striped white and black puffed sleeve on his shoulder, white slashed breeches and white silk hose with tasselled garters, one pale boot pushed far out across the step and the other tucked under, one hand curled loose on the throne arm, a heavy gold fringed cloth hanging down the back of the chair and a red curtain in the dark behind, and learning that jesus was under herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to herod, …
pictures.name: pd_gentileschi_esther_before_ahasuerus

pictures.scene: Bosch, Christ Carrying the Cross — a dark panel packed corner to corner with jeering heads pressed in on every side, the Lord's face at the centre pale and smooth with the eyes closed and the mouth shut, a thorn crown pushed down into His hair and a rough grey beam lying across His shoulder, and crowding round Him a ring of twisted faces, a man in a red cap with his jaw thrust out, a hooded tormentor with a gold earring and a sneering lip, a gap toothed man shouting with his tongue showing, a bald head bent down, bulging eyes and bared teeth and hooked noses turned in at Him from above and below, hands reaching in, a red shield with a chain in the near corner, herod questioned jesus at great length, but he gave no answer, …
pictures.name: pd_bosch_mob

pictures.scene: Netherlandish, The Laughing Fool — a lined old face filling the panel against a flat black ground, split wide in a grin that shows every tooth, wearing a yellow hood with two long drooping donkey ears and a mock crown of red and gold saw points pinned round the crown of it, a white fur collar at his throat and a red and yellow parti coloured coat, one big hand spread flat over his right eye with the fingers splayed so that only the other eye looks out at you, a fool's stick carved with a little screaming head looking over his shoulder in the dark, and a second hand at the bottom holding up a pair of iron scissors, and even herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked him, dressing him in a fine robe, …
pictures.name: pd_the_laughing_fool

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Syndics — five officials in black with wide black hats and plain white collars, ranged behind a table covered by a deep red patterned carpet that fills the whole bottom of the picture, a warm brown panelled wall and a plain tan upper wall behind them, the man at the left leaning in with his lined face turned out at you, the one beside him with a heavy fair fringe of hair opening one hand over an account book laid flat on the table, a bareheaded servant standing between them looking straight ahead, and at the right a long haired member resting both hands on the open page and watching quietly, every face lifted toward the same point outside the picture as though someone had just come in, then pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_staalmeesters

pictures.scene: Zurbaran, Agnus Dei — a young ram lying on its side on a bare grey stone slab against a wall of pure black, lit from the left so that the thick curled white fleece and the clean white face seem to glow out of the dark, the head laid flat on the stone with the muzzle and the pink nose hanging just over the front edge, the eye half closed and quiet, the two pale horns curling back and down past the ear, the body stretched away to the right into shadow, and nothing else in the picture at all, neither has herod, for he sent him back to us, as you can see, he has done nothing deserving of death, …
pictures.name: pd_zurbaran_agnus_dei

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, Prisoners Exercising — a deep narrow prison yard shut in on every side by huge brick walls that climb right out of the top of the picture, the brick laid in green and blue and rust strokes with three small barred windows set high up in it, and down at the bottom a ring of prisoners tramping round and round on the flagstones in a close circle, heads down, hands behind their backs, all in the same worn grey green jackets and caps, one young man in the middle of the front rank with pale yellow hair and a bare head looking straight out of the picture, two warders in dark coats and hats standing watching at the right, and the whole yard sunk in a cold blue green light with no sky in it, barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder, …
pictures.name: pd_gogh_gevangenisplaats

pictures.scene: Breu, The Crowd Cries Out Against Him — a press of men shouting up at someone above and outside the picture, a high priest at the left in a jewelled white and gold mitre and a yellow mantle over a green robe, his eyes lowered and one finger raised as he argues, a second priest bent forward in a scarlet robe with gold embroidered sleeves, a black cap and a white fur collar, his mouth wide open and his throat stretched as he bellows, a bearded elder in a gold crowned mitre at the right staring upward, and behind them a bank of shouting heads in red and green, turbans and caps, jaws dropped and bare arms flung up into the dark, a rolled document in one man's fist and pale stone steps running away in the near corner, but they kept shouting, crucify him, crucify him, …
pictures.name: pd_breu_de_menigte_roept_tegen_hem

pictures.scene: Surikov, The Morning of the Streltsy Execution — a great square at dawn crammed with people and carts, the painted onion domes of a cathedral rising into a pale cold sky behind, condemned men sitting bound in rough wooden carts in their long white shirts, each holding a lit candle that burns small and yellow in the grey light, one black bearded prisoner in a red coat glaring straight out, an old man beside him with his head sunk, soldiers in tall caps with halberds and spears standing over them, women crowding in against the wheels, one in a red headscarf weeping with her mouth open, a little girl in a red kerchief staring up frightened, an old woman slumped on the ground in the near corner with her hands hanging empty, and churned mud under everything, but they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for jesus to be crucified, …
pictures.name: pd_surikov_the_morning_of_the_streltsy_execution

pictures.scene: Bruegel, The Procession to Calvary — a wide bare countryside under a heavy blue grey sky with a black bird turning in it, a strange rock pillar at the left with a windmill perched right on top of it, and streaming across the whole middle of the land a crowd of hundreds walking out to a gallows ring on the far hill, soldiers in red coats on horseback driving the people along, farmers and children and dogs trotting beside them, in the thick of it a man in a pale shirt wrestled off the road by two soldiers while his wife clings to his arm, the beam of a cross tipping over beside him, carts and spears and more riders behind, and down in the near corner a knot of mourners in heavy robes, a woman in white collapsed among the folds of a great red cloak, as they had requested, he handed jesus over to their will, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_procession_to_calvary

pictures.scene: Titian, Christ Carrying the Cross — two heads close together out of a deep brown darkness, the Lord at the right stooped low under the weight with a crown of long thorns pressed into His hair, His face turned up sideways and His eyes rolled back toward the man behind Him, blood on His temple, His shoulder bare and a pale garment slipping down over His back, and leaning in from the left an old countryman with a bald head and a thick white beard, his face full of pity, both arms wrapped round the rough beam of the cross as he takes the load, one broad hand with a ring on it pressed flat against the wood, the great dark timber crossing the whole picture between them, they seized simon of cyrene on his way in from the country, and put the cross on him to carry behind jesus, …
pictures.name: pd_titian_carrying_cross_simon

pictures.scene: Bendemann, The Mourning Jews in Exile — an old man sitting on the ground in a worn red robe under a leafy tree, a gold brown cloth wound round his head, his long white beard on his chest and his face turned away and down, an iron shackle locked round his wrist with the chain hanging loose, his hand resting on the frame of a wooden lyre laid across his knees that nobody is playing, his bare feet on the grass, and leaning against him a young woman with her hair in a thick golden braid, her face hidden entirely in his lap, both her arms wrapped round him, while he lays his hand on her shoulder without looking at her, daughters of jerusalem, do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children, …
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: Courbet, The Forest of Fontainebleau — a huge grey boulder hanging out over the whole top of the picture with its cracked underside in shadow and nothing holding it up, a thin strip of pale sky showing past its edge at the one corner, a tall white barked birch leaning up the left side with its dark twin beside it, and below the rock a steep bank of trees and undergrowth painted in a hundred greens and yellows, leaves catching the light in the middle and sinking into near black at the edges, moss covered rocks sliding down to a still green stream in the near corner that reflects the leaves back dark and broken, and no person anywhere in it, they will say to the mountains, fall on us, and to the hills, cover us, for if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry, …
pictures.name: pd_courbet_bos_van_fontainebleau

pictures.scene: Friedrich, The Cross in the Mountains — a bare rocky summit at sunset seen from below, pink grey crags piled up out of a dark hillside with black fir trees standing round them, and planted on the very top a tall dark wooden cross turned away from us against the sky, the small figure on it hanging with the head fallen to one side, the whole thing in silhouette except where the last light catches it, and behind it a sky of long orange and grey cloud bars with three pale shafts of light rising straight up out of the hidden sun and spreading across the clouds, and no living person anywhere on the hill, two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with jesus, when they came to the place called the skull, they crucified him there, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_the_cross_in_the_mountains

pictures.scene: Huchtenburgh, Casting Lots for a Life — soldiers crowded into the corner of a dusty yard under a high brown rampart, a round stone tower and a thin strip of sky above it, and in the middle of them a drum stood on its end for a table with three white dice lying on the drumhead, a young man kneeling at the right in a loose white shirt that has slipped off one shoulder, his hand still open over the throw and his face turned up wide eyed at the others, a man in a cream shirt and yellow breeches leaning right across the drum pointing down at the dice, a red capped soldier and a hard faced old sergeant with a white beard and a plumed hat watching close, a pikeman's long shaft slanting up behind them, more soldiers in black hats pressed in at both edges, and on the bare ground in front of the drum a heap of thrown down clothes, a black coat and a red cloth lying where they fell, and they divided up his garments by casting lots, …
pictures.name: pd_huchtenburgh_dobbelspel_om_het_leven

pictures.scene: Hals, The Merry Drinker — a broad red faced man filling almost the whole picture against a plain warm grey wall, a huge soft black hat tipped back off his forehead with brown curls pushing out under the brim, his eyes creased up and his mouth open in the middle of talking, a moustache and a little pointed beard, a wide white pleated ruff spread out over his shoulders, a tawny yellow buff coat with slashed sleeves and a gold medal hanging on a cord at his chest, and his right hand thrust out toward you holding up a tall glass of pale wine, the light running round its rim, his other hand lifted open as if he were calling to someone across the room, the soldiers also mocked him and came up to offer him sour wine, if you are the king of the jews, they said, save yourself, …
pictures.name: pd_hals_vrolijke_drinker

pictures.scene: Jacobi, The Halt of the Convicts — a column of prisoners stopped on a muddy road under a wide grey sky with a long ragged line of migrating birds strung across it and a striped black and white milepost standing at the left, and spread along the ground a crowd of convicts in worn brown coats, an old man at the front with a red cap pressing his hand over his eyes, a white faced young man beside him staring at nothing, a woman in a pale headcloth bent over with her arms round a bundle, a fair haired child asleep against her knee and a dark eyed girl sitting up looking out of the picture, a bearded man lying full length at the right propped on his elbow and grinning, guards on horseback with lances ranged along the skyline behind, and in the near corner a heap of leather harness and a long iron chain running away across the ruts, do you not even fear god, since you are under the same judgment, …
pictures.name: pd_jacobi_rustplaats_van_de_gevangenen

pictures.scene: Maes, An Old Woman Praying — an old woman sitting alone at a table in a dark brown room, lit from the side so that her face and her hands come glowing out of the shadow, a white lace cap tied under her chin and a striped white kerchief folded over her black dress, her head lifted in clean profile and her eyes raised toward the light, her lined hands pressed tight together and her fingers laced, a heavy figured curtain hanging down the whole left side behind her, a scarlet cloth covering the table across the bottom with an open book laid flat on it, a pair of round spectacles, a quill and a small dark inkpot, another closed book standing at the edge, a gold embroidered cushion in the near corner and two pink flowers showing in the dark high up at the right, jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom, …
pictures.name: pd_maes_an_old_woman_praying

pictures.scene: Botticini, The Assumption of the Virgin — heaven opened out in wide curved tiers across a sky of beaten gold, rank above rank of angels kneeling and standing shoulder to shoulder in rose and sky blue and white robes, their wings painted red and black and pink, some with hands pressed together, some holding lilies and lamps, and among them the old saints and prophets in heavy cloaks, one cradling a wooden cross, one with a harp, one in a white bishop's mitre, all of them turned inward and upward toward a figure in deep blue at the very top, below the gold a clear empty band of blue air, and at the bottom of the picture a crowd of apostles standing on the grass round a long stone coffin, its lid pushed back and nothing inside it but a mass of white lilies, one bald disciple bending over the edge to look in and the others pressing their hands together or turning to stare up at the opened sky, truly i tell you, today you will be with me in paradise, …
pictures.name: pd_botticini_hemel

pictures.scene: Church, Twilight in the Wilderness — a wild empty country at the moment the sun has gone, the whole upper sky torn across with long ragged banks of cloud burning blood red and crimson over a dark olive ground, one slash of orange low down on the left, a narrow strip of clear pale green and yellow light lying along the horizon with the last white glow of the sun just behind the furthest ridge, blue black mountains folded away one behind another, dark wooded hills closing in on both sides, and down in the valley a still river holding the red of the sky on its surface with a tiny island of black firs standing in it, and not one human figure in the whole scene, the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle, father, into your hands i commit my spirit, …
pictures.name: pd_church_twilight_in_the_wilderness

pictures.scene: Veronese, Christ and the Centurion — a street corner in front of a pale domed building, the Lord standing tall at the left in a rose red tunic and a deep blue cloak, barefoot on the paving, His head bent down and His eyes lowered, an old white bearded disciple and a bald one in pink crowded close behind His shoulder, and at His feet a grey bearded soldier down on one knee in polished steel armour with gold bands on it, a crimson cloak and scarlet hose, one hand still holding his cane, his head thrown right back and his face turned up pleading, a younger officer in a plumed gold helmet kneeling behind him with both arms round his chest to steady him, a halberd held upright in the hand behind, a round shield lying on the stones in the near corner and more helmets and faces pressing in at the far edge, when the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to god, saying, surely this was a righteous man, …
pictures.name: pd_veronese_centurion

pictures.scene: Tissot, The Two Marys Watch the Tomb — a bare white limestone quarry outside the city, ledges and broken cliffs of pale rock stepping down across the whole picture with a dusty track winding through the stones in the near part, a strip of grey sky along the top with a dark olive tree at one corner, and up on the far skyline three empty wooden crosses standing against the cloud, and down on a rock shelf in the middle two women sitting close together, one younger in a dark hooded cloak with her arms folded and her face half hidden, the other older in a white headcloth and a grey mantle with her hands laid in her lap, both of them turned toward the same place below and neither of them speaking, their bare feet in sandals on the stone, and all those who knew jesus, including the women who had followed him from galilee, stood at a distance watching these things, …
pictures.name: pd_tissot_two_marys_watch_tomb

pictures.scene: Hirszenberg, Head of an Old Man — a single old head filling the whole picture against a plain olive brown ground, painted in thick loose strokes, a soft black cap pulled down low over the brow with grey curls escaping at the temples, a long heavy white beard spread down over his chest, deep folds cut into the forehead and dark hollows under the eyes, a strong hooked nose, the mouth hidden in the moustache and set, and his eyes looking down and a little aside out of the shadow of the cap with a tired and steady sadness in them, his dark coat only roughed in below, and nothing else in the picture, he was from the judean town of arimathea, and was waiting for the kingdom of god, …
pictures.name: pd_hirszenberg_head_of_a_jew

pictures.scene: Wright of Derby, A Cavern near Naples — the inside of a great rock chamber seen from within, the roof hanging down dark across the whole top and the left wall rising in huge split ledges of grey and rust coloured stone with a few dry plants rooted in the cracks, the floor a slope of rubble and boulders running out toward the light, and the cave mouth opening at the right in a tall ragged arch on a pale silver sea, a long mountain fading away beyond it, a white tower and a little town on the far shore, soft clouds standing over the water, a thin spray of leaves hanging down over the opening, and nobody inside the cave at all, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid, it was preparation day, and the sabbath was beginning, …
pictures.name: pd_wright_of_derby_a_cavern_near_naples

pictures.scene: Hirszenberg, Sabbath Rest — a plain green walled room in the late afternoon, a tall window in the middle with a white lace valance pinned up over it and pale winter light coming through onto rooftops outside, a brass hanging lamp lowered from the ceiling above it, a small framed picture on the wall at the right, and the household sitting still all round, a man in a dark blue cap leaning back on a chair with a small book held open in both hands and his eyes down on the page, a young woman in a coral pink shawl standing behind the window seat with her head bowed and her hands folded, an old bearded man asleep in a chair at the left with a child curled against him, and in the near corner a woman in a grey shawl seen from behind, bent over a wooden chest with her face turned down, nobody working and nobody speaking, then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes, and they rested on the sabbath, according to the commandment, …
pictures.name: pd_hirszenberg_sabbath_rest

lines.text: Then the whole council rose and led Jesus away to Pilate.
And they began to accuse Him, saying, We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar, and proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King.
So Pilate asked Him, Are You the King of the Jews? You have said so, Jesus replied.
Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, I find no basis for a charge against this man.
But they kept insisting, He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching. He began in Galilee and has come all the way here.
When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
And learning that Jesus was under Herod's jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who himself was in Jerusalem at that time.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased. He had wanted to see Him for a long time, because he had heard about Him and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle.
Herod questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer.
Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.
And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.
That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies.
Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
and said to them, You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined Him here in your presence and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him.
Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing deserving of death.
Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.
But they all cried out in unison: Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!
Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.
Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again,
but they kept shouting, Crucify Him! Crucify Him!
A third time he said to them, What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death. So after I punish Him, I will release Him.
But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.
So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.
As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and handed Jesus over to their will.
As the soldiers led Him away, they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country, and put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.
But Jesus turned to them and said, Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
Look, the days are coming when people will say, Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!
At that time they will say to the mountains, Fall on us! and to the hills, Cover us!
For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?
Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.
Then Jesus said, Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing. And they divided up His garments by casting lots.
The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.
The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine. If You are the King of the Jews, they said, save Yourself!
Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. Are You not the Christ? he said. Save Yourself and us!
But the other one rebuked him, saying, Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.
Then he said, Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!
And Jesus said to him, Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.
It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit. And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, Surely this was a righteous man.
And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.
But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.
Now there was a Council member named Joseph, a good and righteous man,
who had not consented to their decision or action. He was from the Judean town of Arimathea, and was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid.
It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was beginning.
The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.
Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes. And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.
